observed_mechanics: 0x0043cad9 and 0x0043cadd clear the two single-byte override flags at [EBP-2] and [EBP-1] to zero before anything else
0x0043cae4: CMP dword ptr [EAX+0x28],0 - the whole feature is gated on the sub-object at +0x028 being present

0x0043caf0 / 0x0043cafe: CALL 0x004adb80 and CALL 0x004adbc0 with ECX loaded from +0x028; the two callees are one-instruction getters, `return *(undefined1*)(param_1+0x4c)` and `return *(undefined1*)(param_1+0x4d)`, and the results are stored as bytes at [EBP-2] and [EBP-1]
0x0043cb06 clears the [EBP-3] latch, which is set at each of the three dispatch sites (0x0043cbef, 0x0043cc49, 0x0043cdd4)

0x0043cb0a..0x0043cb15: when the +0x4C override byte is zero, 0x0043ce40 is called on the receiver. That function walks the same handle set and calls the same slot +0x30 with the immediates 1 and 1, and only for handles whose flag byte is non-zero - the exact complement of this function's selection.

0x0043cb1a..0x0043cb5c is the first of three identical bounds-checked bit reads. The shape is: MOV ECX,index / CMP ECX,0x3c / JNC <false arm> / MOV EDX,index / SHR EDX,5 / MOV ECX,[EAX + EDX*4 + 0xdc8] / then 1 SHL by (index & 0x1f), AND, NEG, SBB, NEG to turn the bit into 0 or 1. The JNC arm writes 0 into the byte. The 0x3c bound and the word index 0xdc8 + (index>>5)*4 are what identify +0xDC8 as a 64-bit bitset and not a single dword.

0x0043cb24 / 0x0043cb29 / 0x0043cb2f: index 0x19 gives word 0 and shift 25, so the test is bit 25, mask 0x02000000. Bit 25 clear enters the four named handle slots; bit 25 set jumps to 0x0043cc4d and skips them.
0x0043cb6e..0x0043cbf3: the axis-handle loop. The index bound is the literal 3 at 0x0043cb80, the address is [ECX + EAX*4 + 0x154] at 0x0043cb8c, and the null test is at 0x0043cb96.
0x0043cbaf: MOV CL,byte ptr [EAX+0x92] - the per-handle flag byte, cached to [EBP-0x29] and re-read as a dword at 0x0043cbb8

0x0043cbbc / 0x0043cbc0: TEST EDX,EDX / JZ 0x0043cbc8 then TEST EAX,EAX / JZ 0x0043cbf3. The polarity is a disjunction of negations: dispatch happens when the flag byte is zero OR the +0x4C override is non-zero; the handle is skipped only when the byte is non-zero AND the override is clear
0x0043cbde / 0x0043cbe0: PUSH 0x1 then PUSH 0x3, so the two stack arguments in order are 3 then 1

0x0043cbe5..0x0043cbed: MOV EAX,[EDX] / MOV ECX,[EBP-0x6c] / MOV EDX,[EAX+0x30] / CALL EDX - one indirect call per selected handle, thiscall on the handle, two stack arguments, no stack cleanup by the callee

0x0043cbf5..0x0043cc49: the same test against the single pointer at +0x160, with the flag byte at handle+0x5D. Note the opposite branch shape: 0x0043cc24 jumps to 0x0043cc4d (skip) when the byte is non-zero and the override is clear, so the arm structure is inverted relative to the axis loop but the predicate is identical.
0x0043cc4d..0x0043cc8c: the second bit read, index 0x18, i.e. bit 24, mask 0x01000000. Bit 24 set jumps to 0x0043cddd and skips the morph handles entirely.
0x0043cca4 / 0x0043cab3 / 0x0043cab6 / 0x0043cab8: ADD EDX,0x6cc then (end - begin) SAR 2 is the morph-handle count, computed from the two pointers and never by dereferencing the end
0x0043ccc2..0x0043cd02: the third bit read, index 0x0b, i.e. bit 11, mask 0x00000800
0x0043cd0e..0x0043cd1f: the exclusion index is loaded from +0x1B0 only when bit 11 is set AND the +0x4D override byte is clear; 0x0043cd24 stores -1 in the other three cases
0x0043cd67..0x0043cd6f: the loop compares the index against the saved exclusion value and, on a match, jumps back to the increment without touching the element
0x0043cd8e: MOVZX EDX,byte ptr [ECX+0x1d4] - the morph handles carry their flag byte at +0x1D4, a third distinct offset from the two above
0x0043cd97..0x0043cda1: the same disjunction of negations, and the skip jumps to the loop increment rather than to a shared tail
0x0043cdd2: JMP 0x0043cd56 sends the dispatched case back to the increment, so the loop has two tails and no fallthrough into the marker
0x0043cddd..0x0043cde3: the latch is tested and 0x0043cde3 JZ 0x0043cdf2 skips the marker when nothing was dispatched
0x0043cde5: PUSH 0xD0A55625, a 32-bit constant, is the only immediate in the function that is not a small mask or an index
0x0043cdea: CALL 0x004a88d0, whose whole body is `FUN_00435ed0(param_1, FUN_00435e90())`, then ADD ESP,4 - so the callee does not pop and the marker fires at most once per call

semantic_contract: The function walks the handle set of one editor part and pushes a handle state into the selected members. It first reads two override bytes from the part's model sub-object, but only if that sub-object exists. When the first override byte is clear it delegates the complementary half of the work - the handles whose own flag byte is set, with mode argument 1 instead of 3 - to 0x0043ce40. It then visits, in order, up to three axis handles and one rotation-ball handle, skipping null slots and skipping any handle whose own flag byte is non-zero unless the first override byte forces a full sweep; each visit is an indirect thiscall on the handle's vtable slot +0x30 with the two immediates 3 and 1. That whole group is suppressed when attribute bit 25 is set. Next, unless attribute bit 24 is set, it walks the morph-handle array, whose length is derived from its own begin and end pointers, skipping one index taken from +0x1B0 when attribute bit 11 is set and the second override byte is clear, and applying the same per-handle flag rule with the flag byte at a third offset, +0x1D4. If at least one handle was actually visited, it makes exactly one trailing call with the constant 0xD0A55625. It writes no field of the receiver and reads no global. The two override bytes, the three attribute bits and the per-handle flag bytes together form a three-level veto: a global attribute bit can switch off a whole group, an override byte can cancel the per-handle veto for a whole part, and each handle can veto itself.
classification_rationale: All 251 instructions, all fourteen field offsets, all ten constants, both loops, all fifteen branches and the argument order of all three indirect calls are read directly from the disassembly, and the two accessor callees and the complementary-sweep callee were decompiled in full, so the control and data flow are complete. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld on three named bounds. First, the concrete callee of slot +0x30 is never resolved: three call sites share the slot but reach different handle classes, so the operation the handles are being asked to perform is unknown. Second, the owning type is an SDK field-offset correspondence rather than something the binary states. Third, the 0xD0A55625 marker's meaning is not established, because 0x004a88d0 forwards it to 0x00435ed0, which was not analysed.
semantic_findings: The receiver is an editor part: six offsets match the SDK's Editors::EditorRigblock, and the +0xDC8 attribute word behaves as the eastl::bitset<64> the SDK declares, down to the 0x3c bound and the index>>5 word selection.
The two override bytes are read through 0x004adb80 and 0x004adbc0, whose entire bodies are single byte loads, so their offsets are known even though the accessors are not named.

The selection predicate for every handle is a disjunction of negations - visit when the handle's flag byte is clear OR the part's override byte is set - and the same predicate appears three times with three different flag offsets (+0x92, +0x5D, +0x1D4) in two different branch shapes.

The two-argument call is (3, 1) by push order, and the SDK's EditorBaseHandle::func30h(int, bool) at slot 0x30 takes an EditorHandleState first, whose value 3 is Default. That is a candidate reading, not an established one.

0x0043ce40 is the exact complement of this function over the same handle set, with mode argument 1 instead of 3 and the flag predicate inverted, but it is additionally gated on FUN_00401060(), which this function does not consult.

The attribute bits read are 25, 24 and 11 out of a 64-bit word; the out-of-range arm of each read is present and yields clear, so a hypothetical index at or above 64 would silently disable rather than fault.
The function has no side effect on the receiver at all - it is a pure outbound dispatch - and at most one trailing marker call.
unresolved_questions: What does slot +0x30 on a handle actually do? No concrete receiver was ever available, so the effect of pushing state 3 with the flag set is unknown. This is the single largest gap in the reconstruction.

Is 0x0043ce40 really the 'complementary' pass, or an independently scheduled one? It is called only when the +0x4C override is clear, and it consults a global that this function does not, so the two are coupled but not obviously a matched pair.
What is 0xD0A55625? It is neither an address nor a plausible field offset and is forwarded to 0x00435ed0, whose behaviour was not analysed. It may be a profiler scope id, an event id or a hash.
What are the three attribute bits 25, 24 and 11 called? The SDK's EditorRigblock lists mBooleanAttributes as an unnamed bitset with no per-bit documentation.
What do the per-handle flag bytes at +0x92, +0x5D and +0x1D4 mean? They behave as a veto but no SDK field matches, and they sit at three different offsets in three different handle classes.
Why are the +0x4C and +0x4D override bytes on the model sub-object rather than on the part itself? Their role is established only from how they are used here.
The two call sites at 0x005737c7 and 0x005757bd, and the remaining two the ledger lists, were not disassembled, so the frequency and context of this sweep are unknown.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has been captured. A differential run must show which handle classes are actually reached through slot +0x30 and what state 3 does to them.
The three attribute bits and the per-handle flag bytes are only ever read in this build; whether any runtime path sets them, and in which order, needs a trace.
The relationship between this sweep and the globally gated 0x0043ce40 can only be settled by observing both in one run.
